- If sentiment is positive (≥0.33) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) and prices are rising, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2%.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use moving average to smooth.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias in early 30d horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 7d average, reduce by 1–3%.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00) and history shows low volatility, model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next period.
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast for 3–5 days, model is overconfident; apply downward bias of 1–3% for next 3d.
- For 30d horizon, if forecast is >75% of 30d true mean, reduce by 2–5% to avoid overfitting to recent trends.
- If sentiment history includes 1.00 (strong bullish), model often fails to cap upside; cap forecast at 75% above 14d high or 70% above 30d high.
